title: Geranium and ylang ylang soy candle
subtitle: A green-floral soy wax jar candle
excerpt: A floral soy wax jar candle fragranced with rose geranium and ylang ylang essential oils at 7% of wax weight. Geranium gives a green-rosy freshness; ylang ylang adds a warmer, honeyed depth. Pour into a 200 ml glass jar and cure for five to seven days before lighting.
sourceNotes: Rose geranium essential oil flash point: approximately 73°C (supplier SDS, New Directions Aromatics 2022). Ylang ylang essential oil flash point: approximately 70°C. Both are above the 65°C recommended pour temperature for container soy wax. Total essential oil load kept at 7% to avoid wick clogging with undiluted essential oils. Soy wax container formulation from ISTA Mouldings technical guide (2021).

recipe.batchNotes: Pour multiple jars from a single melt. Maintain the 7% fragrance load across all jars.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cure for five to seven days before lighting. Essential-oil candles benefit from a longer cure than fragrance-oil versions, the essential oils bind into the wax matrix more slowly.
recipe.temperatureNote: Pour at 60 to 65°C. Both geranium and ylang ylang essential oils have flash points above this temperature.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years in a cool, dry cupboard out of direct sunlight. Essential oil scent fades faster than fragrance oil, expect noticeable fading after 12 to 18 months.

glossaryTerms.definition: The temperature at which a fragrance or essential oil can ignite if exposed to a flame. Always add oils to wax that has cooled well below the oil's flash point. Rose geranium and ylang ylang both have flash points above 70°C, safe to add at 65°C.
The first burn of a jar candle, which sets the melt pool shape for all subsequent burns. Burn long enough on the first light for the melt pool to reach the jar edge before putting the candle out.
The resting period after pouring. Soy candles benefit from five to seven days of cure before the first light; essential-oil candles may need the full seven days to develop their full scent throw.

items.prepNote: container-grade soy wax; melt in the pouring pitcher
5% of wax weight; add when wax is at 65°C

pre-tabbed cotton wick sized for a 60 to 70 mm jar (CD-10 or equivalent)

content.text: Warm the jar briefly, centre the wick tab in the base, and press it down firmly. Hold the wick in place with the centring bar laid across the rim.

Melt the soy wax in the pouring pitcher over a water bath or low heat. Heat to 75°C to melt fully, then cool to 65°C. Add both essential oils and stir for 30 seconds. Pour slowly into the prepared jar, holding the wick upright. Leave undisturbed until fully set.

Trim the wick to 6 mm after 24 hours. Cure for five to seven days before the first burn. Essential-oil candles develop their full scent throw during the cure, candles lit before five days often smell faint.
